messages:
sasha: Heads-up — after the runtime kernel-selection tweak we rolled yesterday I'm seeing a ~35% p99 latency regression on our 8xA100 replication tests. Nsight timeline shows repeated gaps where an all-reduce seems to wait ~200-400us between microbatches. KV cache hit rate looks stable. Anyone who digs into comm/compute overlap recently?

liam: Yikes. which kernel did we prefer now? fused_attention_v2? Could be different stream sync behavior.

sasha: Yep, autotune picked fused_attention_v2 for seq<=1024. We thought it was faster locally, but at scale things look different.

liam: Can you capture with nsys and nvtx ranges? Include nccl tracing. That helps show whether the stall is before/after kernels or due to NCCL stalls.

maya: Also try NCCL_DEBUG=INFO and set NCCL_ALGO=ring/tree to see if algos change behavior. Sometimes CollNet vs ring changes sync patterns on NVLink clusters.

alex: Add per-rank timers around all-reduce to measure skew — cudaEvent timing is quick to add. Eg:
```python
# add around nccl allreduce
start = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
torch.cuda.synchronize()
start.record()
# call allreduce on default stream
nccl_all_reduce(tensor)
end.record()
torch.cuda.synchronize()
print('allreduce ms', start.elapsed_time(end))
```
That shows if one rank is waiting longer.

sasha: Good call. I ran an nsys capture with --trace=nvtx,cuda,nccl. The timeline shows GPU0 compute finishes, then a gap, then ncclAllReduce call. Meanwhile GPU3 is still running compute during that gap — looks like uneven microbatch finish times creating blocking in the collective.

liam: Could be batching heuristic or shard assignment causing imbalance. Check continuous batching config: are we aligning microbatches across ranks? If one worker has slightly heavier tokenizer/kv workload it can push others to wait.

maya: Also check memory pressure. If auto-offload moved tensors between host and device, page faults or host->device transfers could add tail latency for a subset of GPUs. Inspect per-GPU memcpy in the nsys capture.

alex: For a quick A/B, force the previous attention kernel back and re-run the same workload — if regression disappears, kernel selection likely changed stream ordering or inserted device syncs.

liam: For more metrics use ncu to get kernel occupancy/warp efficiency and L1/shared usage. nvprof is deprecated but sometimes useful for quick CUPTI counters; nsys/ncu combo is better. Also try setting CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 when reproducing to force deterministic ordering for analysis.

maya: Don't forget NCCL tuning knobs: NCCL_TREE_THRESHOLD, NCCL_MAX_RINGS, and enabling/disabling COLLNET if available. On some HW ring/topology the algorithm selection matters more at microbatch sizes.

sasha: Plan I'm running now: 1) full nsys capture with nvtx + nccl 2) per-rank cudaEvent timers + log aggregation 3) run nccl-tests all_reduce to sanity-check bw/latency 4) toggle attention kernel back to previous version 5) try NCCL_ALGO variations and collnet toggle. Will attach captures here.

liam: Also add NVTX ranges around our batching/kv-cache code so we can see if KV cache ops are on the critical path. If KV cache eviction or serialization is happening on the main stream, that could block compute.

sasha: Good point — KV cache hit% looked the same for bulk requests but there might be occasional eviction spikes. I'll add counters and NVTX markers for cache hit/miss and for the prefix cache lookups.

alex: If you suspect comm/compute overlap isn't working, try using ncclAsyncAllReduce (or post ops on separate streams) so communication can start earlier. That needs careful event synchronization with kernels that consume the reduced results.

infra-bot: deploy: inference-runtime commit abc123 rolled to staging at 1749200000.

sasha: FYI I ran a quick nccl-tests allreduce and saw noticeably higher latencies (~30-50us larger) on one node compared to another — suggests topology/NIC differences too. Will try forcing NVLINK-only and measure.

liam: When you post captures, include the nsys summary (gpu kernels table + nccl ops table) and a side-by-side of per-rank allreduce timers. We can script a quick comparator.

sasha: Will do. Uploading links in a bit. Thanks all — posting captures and a short synthesized timeline once I have them. :pray:
